questions.title: "Catastrophic values": What cause them when extending a model’s context window?
questions.question_body:
In section 1 the authors say that introducing position indices beyond the pre‑trained window leads to “catastrophic values” that cause out‑of‑distribution issues.
I’m unsure what exactly these catastrophic values are – are they large numerical spikes in the Rotary‑Positional‑Embedding (RoPE) angles?, numerical overflow errors during softmax?, or something else?
Can someone explain what phenomena occur in practice when a token’s position index far exceeds the range seen during pre‑training?

questions.title: How does Linear Positional Interpolation (PI) differ from NTK‑based interpolation/extrapolation?
questions.question_body:
"Linear position interpolation" simply scales all RoPE rotation angles by a factor equal to the extension ratio $s$.
NTK‑based methods instead impose different scaling factors per dimension based on their frequency.
I cannot see the practical difference – why would scaling higher‑frequency dimensions less and lower‑frequency dimensions more improve long‑context behaviour?
Could someone clarify intuitively what each strategy achieves and why one might prefer one over the other?

questions.title: "Non‑uniformities" in RoPE – dimensions vs token positions
questions.question_body:
"Finding 1" says RoPE dimensions exhibit non‑uniformity while "Finding 2" says initial tokens should receive less interpolation.
What precisely do these two forms mean?
Do we consider frequency groups within individual dimensions or across entire embedding dimension $0$–$d/2–1$?
And how do we determine which token positions belong in “extrapolation mode” versus normal interpolation?

questions.title: Understanding Equation (3): The role of \(\mathbb{I}(\hat\lambda_i,\hat n)\)
questions.question_body:
(3) defines

$$\text{RoPE}_n = [\dots,\, \cos(\mathbb{I}(\hat\lambda_i,\hat n)\tfrac{n}{\beta^i}), \sin(\mathbb{I}(\hat\lambda_i,\hat n)\tfrac{n}{\beta^i}), \dots]\,, $$

with

$$\mathbb{I}(\hat\lambda_i,\hat n)= \begin{cases}1& n<\hat n\\ \frac{1}{\lambda_i}& n \ge \hat n~. \end{cases}$$

Could someone walk through an example – say with a toy dimension $i=0$, $s=4$, $ eta=10000^{2/d}$ – showing exactly how $	heta_0$ would be altered for tokens before and after index $ ar n$?

questions.title: "Search space bounds" in Table 2 explanation
questions.question_body:
(Table 2 ) lists $ eta_i$ search bounds from $1.0$ up to $s	imes1.25$, stepping $0.01$. Where do those limits come from?
Is $s	imes1.25$ arbitrary or theoretically motivated?
Also why allow $ ar n$ only from the discrete set $	set{	zero,	one	wo,	sixteen,	128,	all	ext{s}}$ rather than continuous values?

questions.title: "Monotonicity constraint" $ oldsymbol{λ_i≤λ_{i+1}}$ during evolution
questions.question_body:
(Section 4 ) imposes that every candidate’s scaling factors satisfy

$$λ_0 ≤ λ_1 ≤ … ≤ λ_{d/2−1}\,.$$ 

What theoretical reason guarantees this will never hurt performance?
Is it simply an assumption coming from NTK theory that low-frequency components (high $i$) tolerate larger interpolation?
If a truly optimal solution violated this order would it still be feasible?

questions.title: "Progressive extension strategy" without direct fine‑tuning up to 𝟐𝟎𝟒ₘ
questions.question_body:
(Section 5 ) first learns an LLM with a 256k context window by fine‑tuning on an intermediate length and then performs another search to reach 2048 000 tokens.
My question is:
Why is this two‑step process better than directly attempting to fine‑tune at 2048k?
or perhaps bypassing any intermediate fine‑tuning altogether?
Is it only because datasets longer than ~200 kc exceed practical limits?

questions.title: "Shorter‐context recovery" – dynamic re‑adjustment at inference time
questions.question_body:
(Subsection 6 ) After creating a 2048k model, authors re‑search RoPE rescale factors so that performance at 4k–8k lengths recovers.
Why would one need a separate factor set per short length *during inference*?
Do standard lower‐level attention heads become too “crowded” once scrolled back into very small windows?
and how exactly does LLM decide which factor set to apply?
